A map showing the northern Nigeria area in the early 19th century. To the west and centre is the large Sokoto Caliphate shaded in green. To the northeast, around Lake Chad, is the Kanem-Borno Empire shaded in yellow. A red arrow points from the Sokoto Caliphate eastwards into Borno, representing the Fulani attacks. Two star markers show the locations of Ngazargamu and Kukawa near Lake Chad.

A timeline spanning 1800 to 1900. 1804-1808: Fulani Jihadists attack Borno; Ngazargamu captured. 1814: Al-Kanemi builds Kukawa. 1846: Saifawa dynasty officially ends; Umar becomes Shehu. 1893: Rabeh invades Borno and destroys Kukawa. 1900: Rabeh is killed by the French at Kousseri.
